root_cause.text: `io_wq_remove_pending()` in `io_uring/io-wq.c` updated `wq->hash_tail[]` based only on `io_get_work_hash(prev_work) == hash`, so a non-hashed predecessor (whose hash bits read as 0) could be mistaken for hashed bucket-0 work and оставить a dangling `hash_tail[0]` pointer after the canceled hashed work was removed.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `io_wq_is_hashed(prev_work)` to the predecessor check in `io_wq_remove_pending()` (`if (prev_work && io_wq_is_hashed(prev_work) && io_get_work_hash(prev_work) == hash)`), and the CVE description explains that non-hashed work returns 0 from `io_get_work_hash()`, causing `wq->hash_tail[0]` to be set to a non-hashed `io_kiocb` and later dereferenced after it is freed.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix hash-tail bookkeeping in io_wq removal by ensuring only truly hashed predecessor work items can become the new tail.
intent_record.what: In `io_wq_remove_pending()`, the condition that updates `wq->hash_tail[hash]` was changed from checking only `prev_work` and `io_get_work_hash(prev_work) == hash` to additionally require `io_wq_is_hashed(prev_work)` before treating `prev_work` as the new hash tail.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this prevents an un-hashed `prev_work` from being incorrectly recorded as the tail of a hash bucket just because its hash value matches. The hash tail is only preserved when the preceding work item is actually part of the hashed work chain, avoiding inconsistent list state and incorrect tail tracking.
